thread:
maria: Quick heads-up — CI perf job flagged a p99 spike on streaming with long contexts (>=64k). I profiled and it looks like KV pages are growing and not being evicted until the batch finishes.

aj: Oof. Is this after the recent continuous-batching change?

maria: Yes. We merged the batch-split/merge path to reduce small-batch overhead. After the merge, long-context requests can join and cause the merged batch to keep large KV segments pinned.

devin: Can you paste the profiler excerpt?

maria: Sure — top part of the memory timeline:
```
GPU mem usage timeline (psuedo):
0s: 5.2 GB
0.3s: 7.9 GB (many small requests merged)
0.8s: 12.3 GB (long-context arrives, KV alloc grows)
1.6s: 12.3 GB (batch waits on head-of-line request)
2.0s: drops to 6.0 GB after batch completes

Flame: batching_merge -> kv_pin -> kernel_launch (quantized)
```

kai: So head-of-line blocking: a slow, long KV refill blocks the merged batch and prevents eviction or reuse for other requests. That explains p99.

aj: Do we treat KV pages as per-request or per-shard? We should be able to evict non-shared prefixes while keeping the active head pinned.

maria: Current design pins per-shard pages at batch-level during execution. Merge caused multiple requests with different prefixes to pin more pages simultaneously. Eviction only happens post-batch.

devin: Two quick ideas: 1) split batches by context-length buckets so long contexts don't join short ones; 2) allow incremental eviction within a merged batch using an LRU/age threshold for non-active slots.

kai: Agreed on buckets. Also we can add a "critical" flag: requests that need low latency refuse to be merged with large-context ones. Default low-latency requests remain protected.

maria: I ran a quick sim of bucketed batching — p99 dropped ~30% in the test. But there's a regression: kernel selection sometimes picks a slower kernel when requests are bucketed because it favors a generic kernel for mixed quantization profiles.

aj: That's a separate kernel-selection heuristic problem. We should make kernel selection per-sub-batch after split, not before merge.

devin: Also noticed fragmentation in GPU allocator: repeated pin/unpin sequences for KV slices cause small free fragments, leading to temporary OOM on long runs. We should add coalescing and a background compaction pass when free fragments exceed X MB.

maria: I attached the small reproducer script in CI: `tests/perf/repro_kv_hol.py` — runs many short and occasional long contexts.

infra-bot: CI job 8421 completed — perf regression detected: +12% p99 streaming latency vs baseline. See job link: https://ci.internal/8421

kai: Actionable plan:
- maria: file a perf bug with the profiler outputs + reproducer
- aj: change kernel selection to be post-split (owner?)
- devin: prototype LRU-within-batch eviction + allocator coalescing
- infra: throttle merges by context-length bucket in the short term

aj: I'll own the kernel selection change. Planning a small API: pick_kernel(sub_batch) called after batching split.

devin: I'll spike allocator compaction today. If compaction latency is small we can run it during idle periods.

maria: Filing bug now. Reproducer reproduces the leak in ~30s on our perf instance.

aj: Great. Also add logging around kv_pin durations so we can alarm on long pins (>500ms).

maria: Yep will do. Thanks all — I'll post updates in this thread. :thumbsup:
